messages:
incident-bot: [PagerDuty] alert fired: runtime-p95-high region=us-east-1 service=runtime-inference severity=warning
pagerduty: PD incident #PD-9512 created and paged @eng-oncall
alex: acked — I'll take first look, pulling up p95 timelines and traces
maria: ping — any user-visible errors yet?
alex: initial glance: p95 climbed from ~90ms -> ~480ms around +00:00:12, lasted ~40s. 5xx rate unchanged at ~0.15%
alex: CPU on a small subset of inference hosts spiked; tracing shows long KV cache fills from a single origin host (10.4.8.22)
jun: i'm taking the host (10.4.8.22). sshing now
jun: `journalctl -u workload-proxy -n 200` shows repeated 'kv_load_timeout' and worker threads stuck in gc pause logs
jun: bumped cache warmup workers from 2 -> 6 and restarted workload-proxy: `systemctl restart workload-proxy`
alex: dashboard p95 trending down — now ~110ms and stable for last 20s :white_check_mark:
maria: no increase in user errors or retries, sounds like transient warmup wave, probably due to a model change earlier in the day
sre-lead: thanks. Confirming no requests timed out? any traces showing >5s?
ops-oncall: sampled APM traces — max seen 1.2s, tail only; no customer timeouts or retries above baseline
jun: saved host logs to s3://redwood-ops/incident-logs/PD-9512/host-10.4.8.22.gz; left a note in host: "possible memory pressure from kv loader, follow-up patch required"
alex: creating follow-up ticket TKT-4529 to add better KV backpressure and to instrument cache miss amplification
maria: can we suppress single-host kv warmup alerts? they're noisy and cause churn
sre-lead: Agreed. Proposing alert rule change: require p95 elevation across >=3 hosts for >30s before firing. Filing RFC ops-381 to track
ops-oncall: also adding a short-term alert mute for the host group while we roll a mitigation, will monitor for recurrence during my shift
incident-bot: PD-9512 auto-resolved (no ack timeout) — reason: incident cleared
ops-oncall: handing off to night shift in 15m; i'll watch the host and escalate if we see a recurrence
jun: left heap profile and core dump saved under /var/log/cores/core.2026-03-18 for debugging by runtime-ml team
alex: timeline note:
- 2415550001 alert fired
- 2415550003 alex acked
- 2415550007 identified single-host kv warmup
- 2415550011 jun restarted workload-proxy on 10.4.8.22
- 2415550020 p95 recovered
- 2415550030 pd auto-resolved
maria: linking grafana & traces: https://grafana.internal/d/runtime/p95?orgId=1&from=2415550000&to=2415550040
sre-lead: nice quick mitigation. Marking as 'no-customer-impact' for post-incident report. Follow-ups: TKT-4529 + RFC ops-381
alex: closing thread here — will add more notes in the ticket and ping runtime-ml for root cause analysis
maria: :thumbsup: good coordination everyone
